title: Long BTC — Three-Gate Protocol Activated; All Gates Confirmed July 7
entry: Long BTC $62,500–$65,500 at the July 7 open or on any intraday dip into this zone (BTC at $64,034 per morning briefing). All three protocol gates are confirmed: Gate 1 and Gate 2 (two consecutive UTC midnight closes above $62,000 established the stabilization band) and Gate 3 (IBIT recorded $209M in net inflows as of July 6, confirming institutional accumulation is active, not retreating). Enter 60% of position at or near current price ($62,500–$65,500); reserve 40% to add on any dip toward $61,000–$62,500 that holds the lower gate for two sessions. Do NOT add below $60,000 — two consecutive daily closes below that level would signal the stabilization structure has failed.
stop_loss: $58,100 on two consecutive UTC midnight closes below $60,000 (early warning: single close below $60,000). The $58,100 level sits below the BlackRock IBIT accumulated-cost-basis range and implies BTC has broken through every meaningful near-term support including the three-gate stabilization zone. A single-session dip below $60,000 is possible on the FOMC minutes risk (July 8) — do NOT stop out on a one-day flush if the close recovers above $60,000 within 24 hours. The two-close rule is intentional: prevent a stop-hunt from triggering the exit.
targets: $68,000 — reclaim of the June pre-stop high; three-gate protocol fully absorbed by the market; IBIT cumulative inflows cross $250M week; NFP growth-scare risk diminished; +6.2% from $64,000 entry; cover 35%

$73,000 — FOMC minutes July 8 confirm hike probability is receding on 57K NFP; 10Y pulls back from 4.48%; BTC discount rate compression begins; broader crypto risk-on bid re-establishes; +14.1%; cover 35%

$82,000 — blue sky: FOMC September meeting explicitly removes hike language; BTC re-rates as high-duration asset beneficiary; IBIT inflows sustain $300M+/week for 4 consecutive weeks; institutional rotation out of semis (Kyber delay) partially into crypto; +28.1%; hold final 30%
risk_reward: 1:3.1 to third target (from $64,000 entry, stop $58,100 = risk $5,900; T3 $82,000 = reward $18,000)
catalyst: The three-gate activation protocol is the primary catalyst. Gate 1+2: BTC has posted two consecutive UTC midnight closes above $62,000, establishing a confirmed stabilization band above the prior-cycle stop level. Gate 3: IBIT (iShares Bitcoin Trust) recorded $209M in net inflows as of July 6, the single largest daily inflow in six weeks, confirming the institutional bid is present at current levels. The combination of structural price stabilization plus active institutional accumulation is the systematic confirmation the protocol requires before re-entry. Secondary catalyst: the Korea semiconductor selloff (KOSPI –4.9%, Samsung –7.7%, SK Hynix –6.7%) on the NVDA Kyber NVL144 delay creates a regime of tech/semi distribution that historically produces selective rotation into non-correlated assets including crypto. The rotation is not guaranteed, but the precedent (2022–2025 semi selloffs correlating with BTC accumulation periods) supports the thesis.
thesis:
The June BTC stop-out at $63,500 was a correct, systematic decision: the Warsh FOMC nine-hike dot matrix created a severe discount-rate headwind for a zero-coupon high-duration asset. The stop was right. The re-entry thesis now is different in three specific ways from the June setup.

First, the protocol gates have been confirmed. The three-gate system exists precisely to prevent re-entering a broken trend prematurely. Gate 1+2 (two consecutive UTC midnight closes above $62K) confirms BTC has stabilized above the stop level — not churning below it. Gate 3 (IBIT $209M inflows) confirms the institutional marginal buyer is active. The June conditional opportunity never activated because the DXY gate ($99 requirement) was never cleared — DXY remained at 100.85+. This new protocol replaces the macro gate with an institutional-flow gate, reflecting the evolving reality that IBIT inflows are now a more direct and timely signal of BTC demand than the DXY.

Second, the macro backdrop has shifted. The June 57K NFP print is the most important data point: if the Fed's hike path is constrained by a deteriorating labor market, the discount rate applied to BTC reverses. The BofA 9/18 hike-dot concern that drove the June stop is now tempered by the weakest payroll since early 2020. FOMC minutes July 8 remain a near-term risk, but the minutes reflect the June meeting state — prior to the July 2 NFP. The minutes are hawkish on paper; the market already knows this. The relevant question is whether the September hike is still live, and the answer has materially shifted negative after NFP 57K.

Third, the Kyber NVL144 delay creates an unexpected tailwind. Samsung and SK Hynix collapsing 7–8% on the PCB midplane manufacturing failure removes a significant chunk of near-term AI capex momentum from the equity market. BTC has historically benefited from periods when the 'AI trade' disappoints: capital reallocates from AI-infrastructure equities to non-correlated assets as the hot-money rotates. This is a short-term (2–4 week) tailwind, not a structural argument, but it is relevant for the entry timing.

The bear case is clear: the DXY at 100.85 remains above the old 99 gate. If Warsh's rate framework remains dominant despite NFP 57K, BTC faces continued duration headwinds. The $58,100 stop is wide enough to absorb a FOMC-minutes flush but tight enough to exit cleanly if the thesis is wrong.
bull_case: FOMC minutes July 8 read less hawkish than feared as the committee already anticipated a weak-ish payroll environment; 10Y pulls back from 4.48% to 4.30%; BTC holds above $63,000 through July 8. IBIT inflows sustain $150M+/week for the next three weeks as institutional allocators treat the Kyber delay + Korea selloff as a 'buy crypto, not semis' regime signal. BTC reaches $68,000 (Target 1) by July 18 on the NFP rate-cut re-pricing. DAL Q2 earnings beat July 10 sets a positive earnings-season tone, reducing macro risk-off pressure. BTC continues to $73,000 by late July as the FOMC September hike probability falls below 40%.
bear_case: FOMC minutes July 8 are aggressively hawkish: the verbatim text shows 14/18 members supported rate hike discussion, spooking markets. 10Y rises to 4.65%; DXY spikes back above 102; BTC flushes to $60,500. The single-close rule prevents the stop from triggering, but the recovery fails to materialize: BTC churns between $60,000 and $62,000 for two weeks. On the third week, two consecutive closes below $60,000 trigger the formal stop at $58,100. The Korea tech selloff spreads to US semi names, creating a broad risk-off environment where crypto cannot decouple. Total loss: 9.2% on 5% position from $64,000 entry to $58,100 stop.
invalidation: Two consecutive UTC midnight closes below $60,000 (formal stop at $58,100); OR FOMC minutes July 8 include language explicitly endorsing a July meeting rate hike as a live option (not just September); OR IBIT records three consecutive sessions of net outflows above $100M (institutional demand floor is cracking); OR DXY closes above 103.00 on two consecutive sessions (Warsh framework fully re-embedded, macro regime hostile to BTC); OR BTC breaks below the June 19 stop level of $63,500 on two consecutive closes (would signal the three-gate protocol was a false confirmation)
